name: Agriculture — cme_live_cattle_front_month_settlement covariate forecasting bundle (daily)
link: yfinance LE=F  (CME live/fed cattle front-month, cents/lb)
citation: Yahoo Finance market data via yfinance (CME/CBOT exchange futures settlement prices); Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis archive (daily 2 m temperature); pandas datetime (deterministic calendar covariates)
license: Yahoo Finance: personal/research use of exchange market data (Yahoo TOS). Open-Meteo: free non-commercial/attribution (CC-BY-4.0 ERA5 by Copernicus/ECMWF).
description: Non-EIA, non-benchmark: cattle/feed prices are CME/CBOT exchange-traded futures settlements carried by a market-data vendor (Yahoo Finance), and weather is Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis. No series is sourced from or derived from eia.gov or from a standard forecasting benchmark corpus, so it cannot contaminate a foundation model's training set. Long-format TempusBench bundle for application 'covariate_agriculture_daily_live_cattle_futures'. Target 'cme_live_cattle_front_month_settlement' forecast from 5 covariates. daily cadence, 2887 timesteps, 2015-01-02..2026-07-08. NON-EIA (the foundation model is EIA-trained, so EIA sources are excluded). eia_derived=false.
preprocessing: 1. Download LE=F, GF=F, ZC=F, ZM=F daily via yfinance (interval=1d, auto_adjust, start 2015-01-01, end 2026-07-09 exclusive), one ticker at a time with exponential backoff; cache raw CSVs under datasets/raw/cme_live_cattle_futures_daily/.
2. Extract each ticker's daily Close (settlement); normalize the DatetimeIndex to date; drop duplicate days.
3. Inner-join the four futures on their COMMON trading-day index -> base index (guarantees no futures column is missing at the ends).
4. Pull Open-Meteo ERA5 archive daily Tmax/Tmin at Dodge City KS (37.75,-100.02), timezone America/Chicago, 2015-01-01..2026-07-08; cache raw JSON.
5. Left-join the daily weather onto the trading-day base index (keep every trading day).
6. Interpolate small internal weather gaps (<=3 consecutive) linearly; forward/back-fill any residual edge gaps.
7. Derive deterministic calendar covariates dow (0=Mon..4=Fri) and month_num (1-12) from the date.
8. Order columns [date, targets, covariates], round prices to 4dp and temps to 2dp, dedupe, sort, write wide CSV.
9. Re-read CSV; assert date monotonic-increasing & unique, zero NaN, span>=365d, n_rows>=284.
10. Reformatted wide->long TempusBench (variable_name, variable_unit, timestamps, values); timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; variable names expanded; missing->null; values round-trip-verified against source.
11. Removed calendar/time covariates (day_of_week, month_of_year) from the CSV so the only representation of time is the shared 'timestamps' column.

12. Variable names are written in plain English (underscores replaced with spaces). Target — 'cme live cattle front month settlement' (from source column 'livecattle_close', unit: cents/pound). Covariates — 'cme feeder cattle front month settlement' (from source column 'feeder_close', unit: cents/pound); 'cbot corn front month settlement' (from source column 'corn_close', unit: cents/bushel); 'cbot soybean meal front month settlement' (from source column 'soymeal_close', unit: USD/short ton); 'daily max temperature dodge city ks' (from source column 'temp_max_c', unit: degrees Celsius); 'daily min temperature dodge city ks' (from source column 'temp_min_c', unit: degrees Celsius).

13. Added binary calendar covariates 'is weekend', 'is holiday' (0/1), derived deterministically from the shared 'timestamps' (weekend = Sat/Sun; holiday = US federal holidays). This series covers exchange trading days only, so 'is weekend' is all-zero and 'is holiday' near-zero (markets are closed those days) — near-constant here.
14. Removed the calendar covariates 'is weekend' and 'is holiday' from the delivered CSV.
